description:
`jit-server` started with a relative `--data-dir`, including the default `.jit`, starts normally but answers every storage-backed request with HTTP 500. The default local invocation is unusable, while the Docker image works only because it passes an absolute path.

## Background

Server startup (`crates/server/src/main.rs:68-75`) builds the repository layout with `discover_repository_layout`, which makes the data root absolute. It then constructs `JsonFileStorage` from the raw relative path (`crates/server/src/lib.rs:71`). `JsonFileStorage::configure_repository_layout` returns early when its root differs from the layout's data root (`crates/jit/src/storage/json.rs:1050`). The relative `.jit` never equals the absolute path, so no layout is bound. Every read then fails in `configured_layout` (`crates/jit/src/storage/json.rs:539-545`) with "no repository layout configured for storage reads".

Reproduction:

```sh
cd $(mktemp -d) && jit init && jit issue create --title Hello
jit-server --bind 127.0.0.1:38917 &
curl -s -w '%{http_code}' 127.0.0.1:38917/api/issues   # 500
# same with --data-dir "$PWD/.jit": 200 with the issue list
```

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `jit-server` started from a repository root with no `--data-dir` serves `/api/issues` with status 200 and the repository's issues.
- [hard] REQ-02: A relative `--data-dir` that names a parent or sibling path (for example `../repo/.jit`) serves the same issues as the equivalent absolute path.
- [hard] REQ-03: Storage and layout are built from one normalized data-root path, so a relative and an absolute spelling of the same directory bind the same layout.
- [hard] REQ-04: A regression test starts the server's storage from a relative data directory and asserts that an issue read succeeds.

## Notes

The file watcher (`crates/server/src/main.rs:91`) also receives the raw relative path. Pass it the same normalized path.
title: Server serves storage reads when started with a relative data directory
